passages.text:
## In my projects

<!-- from:ms-pac-man-dqn-readme -->
- [[Ms Pac-Man DQN]]: Experiences go into a replay memory, and batches of 32 are sampled from it to adjust the network. (source: [[Ms Pac-Man DQN README#How the agent works, in plain language|How the agent works, in plain language]])
<!-- /from:ms-pac-man-dqn-readme -->

# Ms Pac-Man DQN

The submitted run trained the DQN agent for 800 episodes, more than doubling the mean score of the untrained baseline from 492.0 to 1032.0. The agent learns by observing stacked grayscale images and receiving rewards based on in-game points. Key tuning involved setting Exploration to 0.10 and increasing Replay Capacity to 15,000.

## Key facts

- The submitted run trained for 800 episodes and more than doubled the mean score of the untrained baseline. (source: [[Ms Pac-Man DQN README#Ms. Pac-Man DQN — Class 3 submission|Ms. Pac-Man DQN — Class 3 submission]])
- Mean score over the five evaluation games for the untrained baseline was 492.0. (source: [[Ms Pac-Man DQN README#Ms. Pac-Man DQN — Class 3 submission|Ms. Pac-Man DQN — Class 3 submission]])
- The trained agent achieved a mean score of 1032.0 over the five evaluation games. (source: [[Ms Pac-Man DQN README#Ms. Pac-Man DQN — Class 3 submission|Ms. Pac-Man DQN — Class 3 submission]])
- The chosen Exploration value was 0.10 to keep genuine exploration while staying closer to evaluation conditions. (source: [[Ms Pac-Man DQN README#My three choices|My three choices]])
- The Learning rate was kept at 0.0001, which was the notebook's reference value. (source: [[Ms Pac-Man DQN README#My three choices|My three choices]])
- REPLAY_CAPACITY was increased from 5,000 to 15,000 because a 5,000-transition buffer held barely 8 games. (source: [[Ms Pac-Man DQN README#Two other hyperparameters I changed, and why|Two other hyperparameters I changed, and why]])

## One limitation

**Five evaluation games is too small a sample to rank agents confidently.** My own results show why:
the per-episode training scores in this run ranged from 130 to 4,400, so a single game says
very little. The gap between run 2 (768) and run 3 (1032) rests on five games per condition, and
seed 101 barely moved even in the winning run. I believe the improvement is real because it shows up
on four of five independent seeds and across two successive runs, but the *precise* mean is not a
stable quantity, and small differences between two agents on this protocol should not be treated as
meaningful. Anything close to this score is, for practical purposes, a tie.

A second, narrower limitation worth recording: `ReplayMemory.sample()` calls
`rng.sample(list(self.items), size)`, which copies the entire replay deque on every sampling call.
Raising replay capacity to 15,000 therefore cut throughput from about 200 to 114 decisions per
second — the tuning that improved learning also made each run substantially slower.

reply:
Based on your notes, here is what changed about the replay capacity in the Ms. Pac-Man project and why:

*   **What Changed:** You increased the `REPLAY_CAPACITY` from **5,000 to 15,000** [3].
*   **Why:** The original 5,000-transition buffer was too small; it "held barely 8 games" [3].

It's worth noting a trade-off mentioned in your notes: while increasing the capacity improved learning, it also made the runs slower because sampling the larger deque took more time [4].

passages.text:
## In my projects

<!-- from:ms-pac-man-dqn-readme -->
- [[Ms Pac-Man DQN]]: Experiences go into a replay memory, and batches of 32 are sampled from it to adjust the network. (source: [[Ms Pac-Man DQN README#How the agent works, in plain language|How the agent works, in plain language]])
<!-- /from:ms-pac-man-dqn-readme -->

# Ms Pac-Man DQN

The submitted run trained the DQN agent for 800 episodes, more than doubling the mean score of the untrained baseline from 492.0 to 1032.0. The agent learns by observing stacked grayscale images and receiving rewards based on in-game points. Key tuning involved setting Exploration to 0.10 and increasing Replay Capacity to 15,000.

## Related concepts

Added during review. Each link says why the two ideas are connected in my projects.

- [[Replay Memory]]: The network is trained on batches of 32 experiences sampled from replay memory. (source: [[Ms Pac-Man DQN README#How the agent works, in plain language|How the agent works, in plain language]])
- [[Exploration]]: The agent mostly picks its highest-valued move and occasionally moves at random; exploration sets how often. (source: [[Ms Pac-Man DQN README#How the agent works, in plain language|How the agent works, in plain language]])
- [[PyTorch]]: The Pac-Man DQN was trained with PyTorch on the Apple M1 Pro's MPS backend. (source: [[Ms Pac-Man DQN README#What the run actually cost|What the run actually cost]])

## One limitation

**Five evaluation games is too small a sample to rank agents confidently.** My own results show why:
the per-episode training scores in this run ranged from 130 to 4,400, so a single game says
very little. The gap between run 2 (768) and run 3 (1032) rests on five games per condition, and
seed 101 barely moved even in the winning run. I believe the improvement is real because it shows up
on four of five independent seeds and across two successive runs, but the *precise* mean is not a
stable quantity, and small differences between two agents on this protocol should not be treated as
meaningful. Anything close to this score is, for practical purposes, a tie.

A second, narrower limitation worth recording: `ReplayMemory.sample()` calls
`rng.sample(list(self.items), size)`, which copies the entire replay deque on every sampling call.
Raising replay capacity to 15,000 therefore cut throughput from about 200 to 114 decisions per
second — the tuning that improved learning also made each run substantially slower.

reply:
Based on your notes, here's what changed regarding replay capacity and the reasoning behind it:

*   **What changed:** You **increased the Replay Capacity to 15,000** [2].
*   **Why:** This tuning change was part of the key tuning involved in training the DQN agent [2].

However, your notes also point out a trade-off related to this change:

*   **The Catch:** Raising the replay capacity to 15,000 actually **cut the throughput** from about 200 to 114 decisions per second because the `ReplayMemory.sample()` function copies the entire replay deque on every sampling call [4].

So, while increasing it was a tuning step that helped learning, it also made each run substantially slower [4].
